title: Ci e Ne Avanzati con l'Imperativo e l'Infinito
subtitle: Combining pronouns, ci and ne with commands and infinitives, including irregular tu forms.
objectives: Attach ci, ne, and combined pronouns correctly to the informal imperative
Apply consonant doubling with the irregular tu imperatives (va', da', fa', sta', di')
Combine multiple pronouns with an infinitive after another verb

content.intro: At this level, pronoun attachment needs to work smoothly even in the trickiest combinations: an irregular tu imperative plus a pronoun, or a chain of pronouns onto an infinitive after a modal verb.
content.explanation: The apostrophized irregular tu imperatives (va', da', fa', sta', di') double the first consonant of any pronoun that attaches to them (except gli): va' + ci → vacci; da' + mi → dammi; fa' + lo → fallo; di' + gli → digli (gli never doubles). With a modal + infinitive, pronouns (including combined ones, ci, ne) can attach to the infinitive or precede the modal — both correct, but the attached form is more common in formal writing.

rules.heading: a) Consonant doubling after va'/da'/fa'/sta'/di'
rules.body:
• Vacci subito! (Go there right away!)
  • Dammi una mano. (Give me a hand.)
  • Fallo per me. (Do it for me.)
  • Digli la verità. (Tell him the truth — gli never doubles.)

rules.heading: b) Pronouns with modal + infinitive
rules.body: Voglio andarci. / Ci voglio andare. Devo dirglielo. / Glielo devo dire. (combined pronoun, both positions correct)

examples.it: Vacci tu, io sono troppo stanco.
examples.en: You go there, I'm too tired.

examples.it: Dammi il tuo numero, ti chiamo dopo.
examples.en: Give me your number, I'll call you later.
Do it right away, don't wait.

examples.it: Devo dirglielo prima che sia troppo tardi.
examples.en: I have to tell him/her before it's too late.
I don't want to talk about it anymore.

commonMistakes.why: The pronoun's first consonant doubles after va'/da'/fa'/sta' — a single c would be a spelling error here.

commonMistakes.wrong: Digli la verità → Dilli la verità
commonMistakes.why: Gli is the one pronoun that never doubles after these irregular imperatives — a genuine, memorized exception.

items.prompt: ___ subito! (Vai lì — irregular tu imperative + ci)
items.explanation: Va' + ci, with consonant doubling: vacci.

items.prompt: ___ una mano, per favore! (Dai a me — irregular tu imperative + mi)
items.explanation: Da' + mi, with doubling: dammi.

items.prompt: "Tell him!" (Digli, or the wrong doubled version?)
items.explanation: Gli never doubles after these irregular imperatives.

items.prompt: ___! (Sta' lì — irregular tu imperative + ci, "stay there")
items.explanation: Sta' + ci, with doubling: stacci.

items.prompt: ___ la verità! (Di' a lui — irregular tu imperative + gli, no doubling)
items.explanation: Gli never doubles: digli.

items.prompt: ___! (Fai questo per me — irregular tu imperative + lo)
items.explanation: Fa' + lo, with doubling: fallo.

items.prompt: Non voglio più ___. (parlarne — pronoun attached to infinitive)
items.explanation: Ne attaches to the end of the infinitive.

items.prompt: Devo ___. (dirglielo — combined pronoun attached to infinitive)
items.explanation: Glielo attaches to the end of the infinitive.

items.prompt: ___ tu, io sono troppo stanco. (Vacci, irregular tu imperative + ci)
items.explanation: Va' + ci, with doubling: vacci.

items.prompt: ___ il tuo numero! (Dammi — irregular tu imperative + mi)
items.explanation: Da' + mi, with doubling: dammi.

items.prompt: Non ___ parlare più. (ne + voglio, pronoun before the modal)
items.explanation: Ne can precede the modal instead of attaching to the infinitive.

items.prompt: Which pronoun never doubles after va'/da'/fa'/sta'/di'?
items.explanation: Gli is the one memorized exception.

items.prompt: Which is the correct doubled form of "fa' + lo"?
items.explanation: The first consonant of lo doubles: fallo.

items.prompt: With a modal + infinitive, where can pronouns go?
options: attach to the infinitive or precede the modal
items.explanation: Both positions are correct.

items.prompt: Which is the correct doubled form of "da' + mi"?
items.explanation: The first consonant of mi doubles: dammi.
Both pronoun positions are equally correct.

items.prompt: Which is the correct doubled form of "va' + ci"?
items.explanation: The first consonant of ci doubles: vacci.

options: I don't want to talk about it anymore.
I don't want to talk to her anymore.
I don't want to talk at all.
items.explanation: Ne here replaces a topic already mentioned.

items.prompt: Which irregular tu imperatives cause consonant doubling?
items.explanation: These are the apostrophized short forms that trigger doubling.

items.statement: Gli is the one pronoun that never doubles after the apostrophized irregular tu imperatives.
items.explanation: This is a memorized exception.

items.statement: Vaci is the correct spelling of va' + ci.
items.explanation: The correct doubled spelling is vacci.

items.statement: Pronouns can only attach to the infinitive after a modal verb, never precede it.
items.explanation: Both positions are correct.

items.statement: Digli means "tell him" and never doubles the gli.
items.explanation: Gli is the exception to the doubling rule.

items.statement: Fallo means "do it", from fa' + lo with doubling.
items.explanation: This is exactly how fallo is formed.

items.statement: These fine points of pronoun placement mark fluent, C1-level control.
items.explanation: Mastering these details is a genuine marker of advanced fluency.

items.statement: Ne and ci can both attach to an infinitive after a modal verb.
items.explanation: Both particles can attach to an infinitive, just like object pronouns.

summary: Va', da', fa', sta', di' double the first consonant of an attached pronoun — except gli, which never doubles.
With modal + infinitive, pronouns (including combined ones) can attach to the infinitive or precede the modal.
These fine points of pronoun placement are a genuine marker of fluent, C1-level control.
